## Goal

Any agent can show what Mostra does, customised to its person: asked "Should I use Mostra?" or "Show me what Mostra can do", it reads the Skill's walkthrough reference (or the project site's walkthrough page, which copies it) and builds, publishes and grows one live page in the person's own scenario (D173).

## Owned requirements

None: a maintenance or design unit owns no requirement (D152). Its progress report's evidence table has one row per item of its scope, each closed by a check through the real public interface (README §3), and the checks it adds extend their owners' rows.

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- `skills/mostra/references/walkthrough.md`, the steps D173 sets out: learn what the person does, build one live page in their scenario, verify and look, publish and hand out the links, wait, read and keep building, and let the person decide; the three ways in, the safety rules and the truth rule;
- its two rows in `skills/mostra/SKILL.md`: "Show what Mostra can do" in the task table and in the references table;
- `mostra docs guide/walkthrough`, registering the reference wherever the guide index needs it;
- a check that fails when the reference names a command or flag the CLI's help doesn't have;
- a site-ready copy of the page's text in the progress report (the project's site lives outside this repository and copies it from there).

Design detail for this package:

- A maintenance unit (D152): it owns no requirement. Its scope is the five items below, each closed with its evidence row through the real public interface; the checks it adds extend the Skill's checks (D162).
- **The reference** `skills/mostra/references/walkthrough.md`: the steps of D173 item 1, in the Skill's own voice and with its own commands, the three ways in (D173 item 2), the safety rules (item 4) and the truth rule (item 5). Use only what the released CLI and Skill do: every command, flag, hook and tool it names must exist in the release it ships with. A step that needs a hosted server says so and gives the local alternative.
- **`SKILL.md`'s two rows:** "Show what Mostra can do" in the task table and in the references table, each pointing at `references/walkthrough.md`.
- **`mostra docs guide/walkthrough`:** the reference is served as the Skill's other references are (`packages/cli/src/docs.ts`); register it wherever the guide index needs it.
- **The command check:** a test that reads the reference, collects every `mostra …` command and flag it names, and fails when the CLI's help doesn't have one, with a seeded command or flag red.
- **The site's copy:** the project's site publishes `walkthrough.md` from this reference (D173 item 3). Put a site-ready copy of the page's text in the progress report: the three ways in, then the same steps in short.
- **Evidence by a real run:** an agent, from a clean home, against the released CLI, runs the reference end to end and publishes a page that passes `verify`; the transcript and both screenshots go into the progress report. Run the hosted path against a reachable hosted server if one is available; otherwise record it as untested and hand it to WP-26.
- Settle D173 item 7's deferred details and record them in the progress report.

## Out of scope

- Templates, the gallery and the docs site (WP-26), which link the walkthrough.
- New CLI behaviour: a gap the walkthrough finds is filed for its owning package, not built here.

## Required reading

Plus the files every WP reads ([README.md](README.md) §1).

- ../DECISIONS.md D149, D162, D167, D168, D172, D173
- ../INTERFACES.md §9 (`mostra docs`), §12 (MCP)
- `skills/mostra/SKILL.md` and every file in `skills/mostra/references/`
- `packages/cli/src/docs.ts` and the Skill's checks (`packages/cli/test/unit/skill.test.ts`)
- WP-14's, WP-30's and WP-31's progress reports
- MT-03's progress report, for a maintenance unit's report

## Acceptance evidence

one row per scope item, each closed through the real public interface: an agent runs the reference end to end from a clean home against the released CLI and publishes a page that passes `verify` (transcript and both screenshots in the progress report); the command check fails on a seeded command or flag the CLI doesn't have; the hosted path runs against a reachable hosted server, or is recorded as untested and handed to WP-26; the prose is accepted with the unit's agent-facing prose (D149).

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- The reference names many commands: the check against the CLI's help is what keeps it true as later packages change the CLI.
- It runs beside another package: touch only the files its scope names, and wait for a merge rather than editing around a file in flight.

## Handoff

Any agent can show a person what Mostra does for their own work; WP-26 links it from the docs site and the gallery.
